definition.hypothesis: If the WorkloadContract, the selected EnvironmentBinding, the versioned platform defaults, and the renderer revision are fixed, the render path produces the same complete claim-relevant release input for the V1 synchronous workload on every render. A claim-relevant contract change changes only the output it owns. Invalid and conflicting inputs are refused with a stable category and code. The release input deploys and serves a real completion, and no claim-relevant workload intent is written again by hand after rendering.
definition.scope: E01 tests the front of the V2 path: contract, render, and release input, and in E01-D also Git, Argo CD, and one served completion. E01 injects no fault and tests no failure tolerance.

outcomeStates.PASSED: Every acceptance criterion of the part held.
outcomeStates.FAILED: The part executed as registered, and at least one acceptance criterion did not hold. A FAILED run is valid evidence and stays recorded.
outcomeStates.INCONCLUSIVE: The part executed and could not answer its question: a check it needs did not run, or its evidence is incomplete.
outcomeStates.REFUSED: The part did not start, because a precondition failed.
outcomeStates.ABORTED: The part started and met an abort condition. The run records the condition and the cleanup.

preconditions: This record, or a later revision of it, is merged. The run records the merged commit it executes, as a full Git revision, and that commit is reachable from origin/main.
The working tree at that commit is clean.
This record is registered in docs/proof/experiments/registry.v1alpha1.json, and its content equals its registered pin.

No material file differs from this record: no pinned input is changed or absent, no file in materialScope is unpinned, and no pinned input is outside materialScope; or a merged later revision of this record classifies each difference. python -m tools.experiment_freeze --changes lists every difference.

E01-A, E01-B, and E01-C only: the runner module and the inferops package the run imports are the ones in the checked-out tree: tools/experiment_e01/core.py and src/inferops. A run that imports either from elsewhere is REFUSED.
E01-D only: every procedure, tool, manifest, and chart file that the E01-D steps name is the one in the checked-out tree at the executing commit. The run executes no copy from another location.

E01-D only: origin/main on the Git remote names the executing commit when the run starts. Argo CD follows main, so a remote main that names another commit is another desired state, and the run is REFUSED.

E01-D only: the environment equals every attribute under identity in fields.environmentIdentity for E01-D. identityVerification in that entry names the step that reads or establishes each attribute. A difference in one attribute that step P3 reads is another environment, and the run is REFUSED. An attribute that a preparation step establishes is verified by the step named for it, and a failed verification also REFUSES the run.
E01-D only: every preparation step of parts E01-D ends with exit status 0. A preparation step that fails ends the run before the Application is applied, and the part is REFUSED.
definition.repetitionRule: No run is repeated to obtain a different outcome. After an INCONCLUSIVE, REFUSED, or ABORTED run, a new run may follow. Every run stays recorded with its outcome state, under its own run identifier.
definition.notResultEvidence: E01-A, E01-B, and E01-C count only when they run, after the record they run under merges, as registered, through python -m tools.experiment_e01 --run in the checked-out tree. E01-D counts only when it runs, after this record merges, as parts E01-D registers it, from the checked-out tree at a merged commit, on the environment this record names. nonResultExecutions lists every other execution that is known and why it is not result evidence. It was fixed when this record was registered, before any E01-D run.
limitations: The platform-defaults revision a release records is asserted. Nothing reconstructs the defaults from it, so the release does not prove which defaults it was rendered from.

The renderer derives the model's download URL and licence reference from the contract's pins by one rule, for one model source. Nothing fetches either URL, so the run does not establish that they resolve.

The material scope's import closure is static: it follows import statements. A module loaded by a name built at run time is outside it; the run records every module file it loaded, and a loaded file outside the pinned inputs aborts the run.
The Python interpreter, the standard library, and installed third-party packages are not pinned by content. uv.lock pins the third-party versions; the run records the Python and uv versions.
Nothing blocks a merge that changes a material file. The precondition refuses the run until a merged revision classifies the change.
The rule against previews is a procedure, not enforced by code.
E01-C-4 is refused by the binding parser, which publishes a code and a field and no rule category.
E01-A, E01-B, and E01-C use one contract on one binding.

No runner and no coded analysis exist for E01-D. A person executes the registered steps and applies the registered verification rules. A driver that transcribes the steps is committed with the run as evidence, and it is not a pinned input of this record. No code computes an E01-D verdict.

tools/experiment_e01 executes revision 2: its CURRENT_REVISION is 2, and it is a pinned input that this revision does not change. A new run of E01-A, E01-B, and E01-C would therefore execute under revision 2 and not under this revision. This revision plans no such run.

python -m tools.experiment_e01 --check reads every directory under runs/ as a static run, and it knows revisions 1 and 2 only. It will refuse the manifest of an E01-D run, which this record puts under runs/ because the review gate reads runs there. The default lane runs that check. So the change that commits an E01-D run must also change the runner's check, after the run. That edit moves a pinned input of this revision and of revision 2, and the repository's static suite builds its temporary repositories from the runner's current bytes and revision 2's pins. A later run of any part therefore needs a later revision that classifies the edit, and the suite needs the runner to know that revision. This was found in review and tried: the edit was made, 13 tests of the default lane failed, and it was taken back out. It is left to the change that commits the run, on purpose.

No command judges a committed E01-D run again from its evidence. The evidence index binds each file that a register record cites by SHA-256, and the review gate compares the review's file digests with the run's files.
The API image digest is not in Git. No InferOps API image is published. The run builds the image at the executing commit and records its digest. Two builds of one commit can have two digests.

The run fills the model cache claim before Argo CD applies the release, from a seed image built on the host from a cached artifact whose SHA-256 the build verifies. The Application's values select the download source, so its acquisition hook is expected to verify the artifact that the claim holds and to download nothing. No registered step reads the hook's job or its log, and Argo CD deletes the job when it succeeds. The run therefore does not observe whether a download happened, and it does not establish that the hook can fill an empty claim.

The preparation release that fills the claim sets the acquisition job's memory limit to 2Gi. On 2026-10-05, on this Kubernetes version, one preparation job was stopped at the chart's limit of 128Mi. The chart is unchanged. The Application sets no such value.

E01-AC9 verifies the model revision by configuration and by content: the runtime mounts the revision directory of the claim, and an init container verifies the artifact's SHA-256 before the runtime starts. A GGUF file does not carry the revision of the repository it came from, so nothing reads the revision from the file.
Argo CD reads the repository from the Git remote without a credential, and verifies no commit signature. Nothing in the run verifies that the commit was reviewed.

The kubectl, helm, terraform, and docker programs, the Argo CD install manifest, the Argo CD images, the Terraform provider, and the base images of the two image builds are not pinned by content in this record. The bootstrap procedure pins the manifest by SHA-256, the Dockerfiles pin their base images by digest, and the run records the tool versions.
The material scope lists each shell procedure by path. A file that a pinned procedure starts to read is in the scope only when a path or pattern of the scope names it.

The cleanup removes the Application, Argo CD, the namespace, and the claim. It does not remove images from the node or from the host: the API image, the model seed image, the runtime image, and the Argo CD images stay.

The verification rules of E01-AC10 are the measure of 'restates or overrides': the admission check and the eight-character comparison. A hand-written value that names the same thing in other characters, such as the runtime's model alias, is not a finding of either rule.
E01-D uses one contract, one binding, one cluster with one node, and one run.

definition.previewRule: No full execution of E01-A, E01-B, and E01-C is exempt from being an attempt. A development preview, a dry run, or a run in a throwaway repository is not permitted under this revision. If one happens, it is reported in the next run's validation record with what it executed and what it showed, and it is never presented as preregistered. This rule is a procedure: no code can stop a run outside this repository, and this record does not claim that one does. For E01-D, from the registration of this record: an execution on the named environment that applies the Application and sends a completion, before the first E01-D run of record, is an E01-D attempt. It is recorded under its own run identifier with its outcome state. A rehearsal is not permitted. This is also a procedure, and no code enforces it.
definition.executionIdentity: The run records the merged commit it executes and the origin/main revision it checked against; the content digests of this record and of the registry; where the runner and the inferops package were imported from, and the inferops distribution version; and every repository module file the run and its second process loaded, with its content digest. A loaded file that is not a pinned input with its pinned content is an abort condition. An E01-D run records: the executing commit and the commit that origin/main names on the remote; the content digests of this record and of the registry; the output of python -m tools.experiment_freeze --changes for this record; each attribute of the environment identity as the run read it; the versions of kubectl, helm, terraform, docker, uv, and Python; the digest of the API image and of the model seed image that the run built; and the commit that Argo CD reports that it resolved and applied.
definition.selfReference: A record cannot contain the digest of a file that contains the record's digest, and it cannot name the commit that merges it. So this record does not pin the registry, which pins this record; the registry is data, not code, so the freeze checker that the run imports is pinned here without a cycle. The run records the registry's digest and the merged commit it executes instead. pinnedInputs fixes the experiment path; gitRevision.preparedFrom names the commit the record was prepared from, not the commit that merges it.
definition.revisionPurpose: This revision names the environment of E01-D, the Git desired-state path, and the Argo CD Application, and it registers the steps and the verification rules of E01-D. It pins the files of that path. It changes one clause of one criterion, E01-AC10, and criteriaChanges states the change. procedureChanges and fieldChanges list every other statement about E01-D that differs from revision 2. For E01-A, E01-B, and E01-C the parts and the criteria are those of revision 2, and so is every field entry except two that cover all four parts: experimentIdVersion, which now names revision 3, and gitRevision, which names the commit this record was prepared from. Every pinned input of revision 2 has the content revision 2 pinned.

staticResultConsumed.statement: This revision consumes the second run of the static parts as the static result of E01. It does not run them again, and it does not judge that run again. That run answers revision 2.
staticResultConsumed.whyStillValid: No pinned input of revision 2 has other content at the commit this record was prepared from, and the change that registers this revision edits none: python -m tools.experiment_freeze --changes for revision 2 reports no difference. inputChanges lists no changed input and no removed input. Every entry is a file this revision pins for the first time.
staticResultConsumed.whatE01DTakesFromIt: E01-AC5 of that run holds that admit_manual_values admits the hand-written values fixture, tests/domain/fixtures/helm-values/support-assistant-local.manual-values.yaml, with no finding, and that no string in the fixture contains a workload-intent generated value of eight characters or more. The verification rule of E01-AC10 uses that verdict together with a test that holds the Application's hand-written values equal to the fixture without its API image digest.

reviewGate.statement: An E01-D result enters the claim and evidence register only through a ledger that names one independent review artifact of that E01-D run, under docs/proof/experiments/v2-e01/reviews/. tools/evidence_index refuses a ledger that bears on a run and names no review of it, a review whose file digests are not those of the run's files, and a review that names another freeze record than the run's manifest names.
reviewGate.notReused: docs/proof/experiments/v2-e01/reviews/20261003-e01-abc-1-review-1.v1alpha1.json reviews the second static run. It is not a review of an E01-D run, and the gate refuses it for one.
reviewGate.manifest: The gate reads metadata.freezeRecord from the run's run.v1alpha1.json. An E01-D manifest names this record there, by repository path, with its content digest in metadata.freezeContentSha256.

parts.title: Deterministic double render
parts.question: Do two renders of identical inputs produce identical release input that records its sources?

inputs.platformDefaults: Version v1alpha1: the requestTimeoutMs, drainTimeoutMs, and maxOutputTokens values of the api block of charts/inferops-llm/values.yaml, read as tools/generated_release reads them.
inputs.renderer: HelmValuesRenderer from src/inferops/domain/render, constructed with the executing commit as its revision.

procedure: Load the compatibility matrix. Parse the contract with parse_workload_contract and the binding with parse_environment_binding.

Call generate_release with the renderer, the contract, the platform defaults, the binding, and binding_name local-kind. generate_release validates the contract and builds the render context before it renders.
Write the result with write_release to render-a, a directory that does not exist before the call.
In a second Python process, with a different PYTHONHASHSEED, repeat the three steps above and write to render-b.
Compare render-a with render-b: the bytes of values.generated.yaml, the bytes of rendered-workload-release.yaml, the SHA-256 of each file, and metadata.releaseId.

Check the provenance of render-a against values computed apart from the release: source.contract.sha256 against contract_digest of the parsed contract; the source.environmentBinding name, apiVersion, and sha256 against local-kind, inferops.io/v1alpha1, and binding_digest of the parsed binding; output.helmValues.sha256 against the SHA-256 of the bytes of render-a/values.generated.yaml; source.renderer.revision and source.platformDefaults.revision against the executing commit.
Admit the hand-written values beside the render-a values with admit_manual_values.

List every chart value that a workload-intent context value renders to, from HELM_VALUE_DISPOSITIONS and RENDER_FIELD_OWNERSHIP, and every chart value DERIVED_HELM_VALUES derives from workload-intent context values only. Check that each is in render-a/values.generated.yaml.

Merge the chart's defaults, render-a/values.generated.yaml, and the hand-written values the way Helm merges values files. Merge the chart's defaults and the V1 real values the same way. List every value that differs.
For every string in the hand-written values, list each value from the previous step that is at least eight characters long and occurs in it.

parts.title: Intent mutation
parts.question: Does one claim-relevant contract change move only the output it owns?
parts.rationale: The runtime replica count is claim-relevant workload intent with a known deployment effect. The chart runs a fixed replica count, so the range is set to one number, inside the chart's limit of 16.
procedure: Apply the mutation, as JSON Patch operations, to the contract document as read from YAML, before parse_workload_contract.
Render and write as in E01-A steps 1 to 3, to mutation, a directory that does not exist before the call.
Compare mutation with render-a of the same run: list every leaf of values.generated.yaml that differs, with both values, and every field of rendered-workload-release.yaml that differs.
Check that source.contract.sha256 in mutation equals contract_digest of the mutated contract.

parts.question: Are invalid and conflicting inputs refused deterministically, with the expected stable category and code?

inputs.cases: The cases below. An edit is a JSON Patch operation, applied to the document as read from YAML before it is parsed. An input a case does not list is the E01-A input.

procedure: For each case, build its inputs from the pinned files and the edits it lists.

Run the step the case names. For generate_release and parse_environment_binding, parse the inputs and call generate_release as in E01-A. For admit_manual_values, call it with the values of the E01-A render and the edited hand-written values.
Record the refusal: its exception type, and for each finding in order, its rule identifier, category, code, and field. For a refusal with no findings, record its code and field.
Check that the case's output directory does not exist after the case.
Run each case a second time in the same way, and compare the two refusals.

parts.title: Real deployment
parts.question: Does the release rendered from the unmodified contract deploy through Git and Argo CD and serve a real completion?

inputs.workloadContractStatement: The unmodified reference contract, as revision 2 registered.
inputs.renderer: HelmValuesRenderer from src/inferops/domain/render, in the checked-out tree, called through tools/gitops_desired_state.

rendererRevision.statement: The release records this commit as its renderer revision and as its platform-defaults revision. tools/gitops_desired_state declares it. It is the commit that the change that added the release was based on.
rendererRevision.differenceFromRevision2: Revision 2 gave the E01-D renderer as E01-A's: constructed with the executing commit as its revision. A release cannot name the commit that adds it to Git, so a release that is accepted into Git never records the commit that Argo CD applies. The run derives the release again at the executing commit, with the declared revision, and compares it with the committed release byte for byte. No criterion of E01-D names the renderer revision. E01-AC4 names it for E01-A only.

messages.content: Reply with the single word: ready

request.through: A kubectl port-forward to port 8090 of the Service inferops-inferops-llm in the namespace inferops-release.
request.retry: None. A request that returns no response, or a status other than 200, is the result.

procedure.action: Derive the release from the contract, the binding, and the platform defaults at the executing commit, and compare it with the committed desired-state release, byte for byte.

The release is in the executing commit, which origin/main names. The run commits no release and changes no file under gitops/. Record the blob identifier and the SHA-256 of each of the two files at the executing commit in release.json.

procedure.frozenStep: Let Argo CD reconcile the desired state into the cluster. The release takes its values from the generated values file, from the Application's hand-written values, and from the one parameter api.image.digest. The run supplies no other parameter.
procedure.action: Apply the project and the Application with the digest that step P4 printed. The procedure waits a bounded time until Argo CD reports a succeeded sync operation at the commit that main names. Then compare the live objects with the committed manifests.

procedure.frozenStep: Wait until the API's readiness endpoint answers 200 and the runtime pod is Ready. The wait is bounded by the startup budget the chart renders for the runtime, counted from the moment Argo CD reports the desired revision synced.
procedure.action: Record the time at which the apply of step D3 returned: the procedure returns when Argo CD reports a succeeded sync operation at the commit that main names. One deadline applies to both waits: 600 seconds after that time, the startup budget that the chart renders for the runtime. Wait for the rollout of the runtime Deployment, and then for the rollout of the API Deployment, each with the seconds that remain to the deadline as its timeout. Then request the API's readiness endpoint once, through a port-forward to the API Service.

kubectl --context docker-desktop rollout status deployment/inferops-inferops-llm -n inferops-release --timeout=<seconds-remaining>s
procedure.expected: Both rollouts complete before the deadline, and the readiness request returns 200.
procedure.whenNot: A rollout that does not complete before the deadline, or a readiness request that does not return 200, is recorded. No completion is requested, E01-AC8 does not hold, and the part is FAILED, unless an abort condition applies.

procedure.frozenStep: Send one request to the API Service: POST /v1/chat/completions, with model set to the generated model.identifier, one user message, and stream false.
procedure.action: Send the registered request once, through the same port-forward. The command writes the response body to a file under .artifacts/, which Git ignores, and prints the HTTP status. From that file and that status, write to completion.json: the request, the HTTP status, the response's model, the number of choices, the finish reason and the length of the assistant message of the first choice, and the usage counts. The response file is not committed, and the generated text is not kept.
commands: curl --silent --show-error --max-time 300 --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"model":"qwen3-1-7b-q8-0","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with the single word: ready"}],"stream":false}' --output .artifacts/e01-d/<run-id>.completion-response.json --write-out '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:<local-port>/v1/chat/completions
procedure.expected: One HTTP status, and one response body or none. They are the observation that E01-AC8 judges. A request that returns no response is recorded with the status that curl prints and with curl's exit status.

kubectl --context docker-desktop get pods -n inferops-release -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=inferops -o json

verification.statement: How each E01-D criterion is judged. A rule that does not hold makes its criterion not hold, and the part is FAILED. When a step was executed and its evidence file is absent or cannot be read, the part is INCONCLUSIVE, and nothing is inferred in place of the observation. Step D4 states its own outcome rule.
E01-AC8: completion.json records HTTP status 200 for the one request of step D5.
The response holds at least one choice, and the assistant message of the first choice has a length greater than 0.
The release that served it is the one of steps D1 to D3: the rules of E01-AC9 hold.
E01-AC9: Synced revision: in argo.json, status.sync.status is Synced, status.sync.revision is the executing commit, and status.operationState.phase is Succeeded with status.operationState.syncResult.revision equal to the executing commit.
